theoretical_nodes.description: Theoretical nodes constructed from the hypothesis graph. These are new constructs that emerge from patterns among reduced categories — not pre-existing clusters to be verified.

node_label.description: Theoretical label expressed as a {label_name}, 2-6 words. Captures the emergent theoretical construct (e.g., 'Navigating Uncertainty', 'Maintaining Professional Identity').

theoretical_family.description: The theoretical code family that best describes this node's organizing logic (e.g., Strategy, Causal, Process, Condition, Consequence).

constituent_categories.description: The reduced categories that form this theoretical node.

emergence_rationale.description: WHY this node emerges: what hypotheses connect these categories? What pattern do they collectively reveal? Reference specific hypothesis evidence.

description.description: 2-4 sentence narrative describing what this theoretical node captures and its significance to the emerging theory.

relationship_to_core.description: How this theoretical node relates to the core category. Describe the nature of the connection using theoretical language grounded in the evidence.

isolated_categories.description: Categories that did not form part of any theoretical node.

reason.description: Why this category did not form part of any theoretical node (no hypotheses, insufficient evidence, conceptually disconnected).

bridging_nodes.description: Theoretical nodes that connect two or more other theoretical nodes.

connects_nodes.description: Labels of theoretical nodes this bridging node connects.

bridging_rationale.description: How this node bridges the connected theoretical nodes. What theoretical relationship does it establish between them?

theoretical_playground_guidance.description: Guidance for the Theoretical Playground: which theoretical nodes to elaborate first? What gaps suggest new data collection? How should the researcher prioritize theoretical development?
